bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delays in Tower 2 commencement due to litigation over approvals; WSA site execution delays due to land acquisition or state-level bureaucracy; competition in premium office space from new Mumbai supply; margin compression in BEC if demand softens
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, visionary, and disciplined; emphasizes long-term value creation over leverage; acknowledges debt potential but prioritizes safety; proactive on ESG and digital adoption; responsive to shareholder feedback on virtual AGMs
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Wayside amenities (WSA) are not just fuel stops but integrated experience hubs with F&B, retail, and hospitality — a defensible moat in rural-urban corridor development; Nesco’s 100% green power (not solar) is sourced via PPAs, making it a rare ESG leader in real estate without rooftop panels
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Nesco Realty: Tower 3 & 4 at 100% occupancy; Tower 2 (IOD secured) to add 1.6M sq.ft IT + 750-room hotel; BEC: Rs.175cr revenue, 50%+ EBITDA margin, Hall 6 operational; Nesco Foods: 16% growth, 50+ brand partnerships; Indabrator: Rs.50cr revenue, 3 WSA tenders secured; WSA: 11 sites awarded (4 Hyderabad-Vizag, 3 Bangalore-Chennai, 4 Raipur-Vizag), 8-10% blended margin

outlook.body: revenue growth: >20% CAGR over 3-5 years (driven by Tower 2, WSA, BEC); margin: target 65%+ EBITDA margin across new verticals; order inflow: 11 WSA sites secured (Rs.100cr/site revenue potential); capex/commissioning: Rs.3,500cr over next 5 years, Tower 2 construction to commence late FY26, WSA sites to commission Q4FY27-Q1FY28
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.3,500cr total capex commitment: Rs.3,500cr for Tower 2 (IT + hotel) + Rs.1,100cr implied capex for 11 WSA sites (Rs.100cr/site avg) = Rs.4,600cr total project pipeline
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into 50+ additional highway corridors; REIT listing of Tower 2 or BEC assets; franchising Nesco Foods model; scaling Indabrator’s WSA tech platform to third-party operators
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Nesco has accelerated its transformation from a Mumbai-centric real estate player into a multi-vertical experience economy operator, with major new revenue streams from highway wayside amenities and Tower 2’s integrated hotel-office complex now on the cusp of execution, fundamentally reshaping its growth profile and valuation drivers.

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 7.00 per equity share (face value Rs 2) for FY26, subject to AGM approval, up from Rs 6.50 per share in FY25.
Wayside Amenities development begins on 4 sites across the Hyderabad-Visakhapatnam expressway corridor, out of 9 sites in possession across 3 corridors.
Wayside Amenities is in its development stage with no operating revenue in FY26; revenue is expected to begin in the later part of FY 2026-27 as sites become operational.
Construction has begun on four sites of the Hyderabad–Visakhapatnam Expressway (Khammam–Devarapalli Section), out of 9 sites across express corridors awarded via 3 NHLML tenders.
Development of Tower 2 at Nesco IT Park, for which the Intimation of Disapproval (IOD) has been received, will add premium office space and a large hotel facility.
Planned redevelopment of Bombay Exhibition Center halls into state-of-the-art, pillar-free spaces to enhance functionality and customer experience.
Capital expenditure for the planned expansion (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, Wayside Amenities) is planned to be funded entirely through internal accruals, maintaining the debt-free balance sheet.

Indabrator plans to grow its order book while running leaner — building out its marketing team to widen the pipeline and staying selective on orders, favouring those with clear execution and healthy margins.
The in-house Décor service line's longer-term aim is to grow serving clients beyond the Nesco campus.

As the business enters a more capital-intensive cycle (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, WSA), management's focus remains on prudent capital allocation and efficient deployment of resources while preserving the debt-free balance sheet.

Tower 2 at Nesco IT Park (5.01 mn sq. ft. total constructed area; 2.50 mn sq. ft. chargeable premium office space, plus an integrated 700+ room hotel and 150+ serviced apartments) is cleared to proceed following receipt of the IOD; construction is to commence immediately on final clearances, with an expected duration of about 60 months from commencement, funded through reserves and accruals.

risks.note: The Company operates across six structurally distinct verticals — commercial real estate, exhibitions, events, hospitality and food services, engineering and wayside amenities — each with its own risk profile, cyclicality and external sensitivities. Governing this mix requires the Company to run a formal Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework embedded across every business unit, aggregating heterogeneous exposures (strategic, operational, compliance and financial, each rated high/medium/low by probability and impact) that would otherwise be managed as separate businesses.
